subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC network qualification (ACME)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Lily Tan <lily.tan@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC network qualification (ACME)

Thanks for the call earlier today — great discussion. Recap below and proposed next steps so we can scope a Private/VPC deployment that meets ACME's latency and throughput needs.

Key performance goals you stated:
- Tail latency target: P95 < 120ms for single-request streaming (in-region).
- Throughput: 1,200 requests/minute sustained (peak 2,500 requests/minute).
- Concurrency: expected active concurrency 60–100 concurrent streams during peak.
- Streaming requirement: server-side chunked streaming for partial responses (low-latency token streaming).

Private/VPC / network items we need to qualify:
1) Network path: Do you plan to use AWS VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, or site-to-site VPN to connect to Redwood Private?
2) Egress requirements: Any egress filtering or proxying that could add latency (e.g., egress through a centralized NAT/proxy)?
3) Internal latency budget: What is your internal application-to-ingress budget (ms) between your service and the VPC endpoint?
4) MTU / packet loss tolerances and expected RTT between your app and the Redwood edge in your region.
5) Will you want dedicated peering for predictable latency or use shared interconnect?

Attachments requested from ACME so we can baseline: network topology diagram (showing peering/VPN), recent perf test/latency measurements to our endpoint (if available), and any proxy/firewall rules that might impact long-lived streaming.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Samir/Lily: share a network diagram and any perf traces (target by EOD Thu).
- Aditya: schedule a technical deep dive (30–45m) next week for packet/peering discussion and to run a small streaming test.
- Jordan & I: prepare an SLO matrix (we attached a draft) that maps your goals to config suggestions (batching/kv-caching/instance sizing).

If the targets above are accurate, we can prepare a small scoped POC on a Dedicated/Private deployment to validate P95 and concurrency under your traffic shape.

Thanks — looking forward to the network artifacts.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lily Tan <lily.tan@acme.com>, ACME IT Ops <it-ops@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC network qualification (ACME)

Thanks, Marissa — great recap. Confirming the targets are accurate for our initial phase. Quick answers to the network items:
- We plan to use AWS Transit Gateway for cross-account peering to Redwood's VPC (preferred for routing flexibility).
- Egress flows currently go through a central proxy for outbound inspection; we can route traffic for Redwood endpoints via a dedicated egress rule to reduce extra hops.
- Internal app-to-VPC endpoint budget: target < 30ms one-way.
- Average RTT to the us-west-2 region (from our primary app cluster) is ~12–18ms; current packet loss negligible (~0.01%). MTU standard 1500.
- We'd prefer dedicated peering for predictable latency if Redwood supports it — happy to discuss pricing implications.

I've attached our network diagram and a short perf trace from yesterday's synthetic load test. Let us know if you need more detail.

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf (application/pdf), acme-synthetic-trace.zip (application/zip)

Samir
Sr. Director, Platform Engineering
ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC network qualification (ACME)

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed, thanks for the quick turnaround. I reviewed the diagram and trace at a high level; next items from our side: 

- Aditya, can you take point on a technical deep dive? Suggested agenda: walk the transit gateway peering options, verify egress path and proxy bypass for Redwood endpoints, and run a streaming micro-benchmark to validate P95 at target concurrency.
- Jordan & I will map the ACME numbers to instance sizing and batching parameters (we'll include options: low-latency config vs cost-optimized).
- Samir/Lily: could you confirm an internal contact for network changes (ticket owner) and preferred time window for a short tests (we prefer off-peak but can run during a controlled peak window if you prefer).

Proposed slots next week: Mon 2028-03-26 09:00-09:45 PT or Tue 2028-03-27 13:00-13:45 PT. Aditya, Jordan — can you confirm availability?

We'll also prepare a brief POC plan (1–2 day test) that uses a dedicated peering path and a small fleet to exercise streaming concurrency. If the micro-benchmark shows any regression we can iterate on placement and kernel configs.

Thanks —
Marissa
